chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Maṭar narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“Indeed, false witnesses are flogged with a punishment that has no fixed limit; that is up to the Imam. And they are paraded until the people recognize them. And His saying, Mighty and Majestic, is:”
“And do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the transgressors, except those who repent.”

I said: “By what is his repentance recognized?” He said: “He declares himself false before the heads of the witnesses where he is punished, and he seeks forgiveness from his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. So if he does that, then his repentance has become manifest.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority who determines the punishment here
key_terms.الْفَاسِقُونَ: those deemed openly sinful or transgressive
key_terms.تَوْبَتُهُ: his repentance and return from wrongdoing
key_terms.حَدًّا: a penal punishment imposed in law
key_terms.شُهُودَ الزُّورِ: false witnesses who knowingly give untrue testimony
key_terms.يُجْلَدُونَ: they are flogged as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: How is the repentance of a false witness recognized in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal and public consequences for false testimony, including discretionary flogging and public exposure determined by the Imam. It also explains that the witness’s repentance is recognized through public self-retraction and seeking forgiveness from Allah عزّ وجلّ.
